fin.internationalNote: Santa Monica College F-1 international cost $25,658 (2026-27, Tier-1 verified from SMC's official International Student Tuition & Fees page for Fall 2026 - Summer 2027): non-resident tuition $486 a unit × 24 units = $11,664 + SMC health $56, Associated Students resource $20, student benefits $45 and student representation $4 = $125 in fees + SMC's published living-expenses allowance $13,869. NO credit-load assumption was needed — SMC states the basis itself (24 units across 2 semesters, the F-1 minimum of 12 a semester). ⚠ READ THE HOUSING LINE CAREFULLY: SMC has NO on-campus housing at all, so the $13,869 is NOT billed by the college — it is SMC's own 9-month living-expenses estimate based on a HOMESTAY WITH TWO MEALS A DAY, and SMC's page says a student with free room and board locally may deduct it in full. It is stored under `roomBoard` because a player still has to live somewhere and a tuition-only figure would badly understate the real outlay. Mandatory F-1 health insurance ($2,310) is excluded by convention, as are books ($1,064) and personal expenses ($4,968); SMC's own total for the year is $34,000. The previous stored $9,000 was an unresearched ballpark and understated the cost by $16,658 — nearly threefold, the largest PROPORTIONAL error in the campaign. As a CCCAA program Santa Monica cannot offer athletic scholarships at all, so this figure is very close to what is actually paid.

culture.vibe: Community college culture — diverse, no-nonsense, goal-oriented. Santa Monica College is famous for transfer students who are serious about getting to UCLA or another UC. The campus is workmanlike but Santa Monica itself is extraordinary.
culture.thingsToDo: Santa Monica Pier and beach (literally adjacent to campus), Venice Beach boardwalk (2km), Third Street Promenade shopping, Abbot Kinney Boulevard, LA access via Metro, Santa Monica Mountains hiking. Campus is 100m from the Pacific Ocean.
culture.socialScene: Extremely diverse — ages, nationalities, backgrounds. No campus residential culture — students come, learn, and go to the beach. Transfer focus means peers are academically motivated. Very accepting and unpretentious.
culture.olivierMatch: ★★★★★ Santa Monica is arguably the most Sydney-like location in America. Ocean, surf culture, warm year-round, diverse, laid-back. For a 2-year stay while building GPA, the lifestyle is extraordinary. Campus culture is secondary to location culture.
culture.lifestyleTags: Beach lifestyle, transfer focus, Sydney-like

facilityDetails.academicLabs: SMC Kinesiology Department: anatomy and physiology teaching labs, computer exercise physiology suite. UCLA's transfer pathway means students who thrive at SMC often access UCLA's world-class labs from Year 3 — the JUCO → UCLA lab upgrade is significant.
facilityDetails.extras: Santa Monica Beach (100m from campus — not a typo). Venice Beach boardwalk (2km). Third Street Promenade. Santa Monica Pier. Entire LA accessible by Metro Expo Line from campus. Google, Apple, and major tech campuses in Santa Monica for career networking. The best JUCO location in America.

housing.note: Santa Monica College has no on-campus student housing at all. Students arrange their own accommodation in the surrounding area — SMC provides housing search resources but no dorms.

fin.internationalNote: Miami Dade non-resident cost $27,812 (Tier-1 verified from MDC's official Tuition & Fees rate table and its published Cost of Attendance chart, Associate programs / Non-Resident / Students Living Independently): tuition and out-of-state fee $331.11 a credit × 24 credits = $7,947 + student services, financial aid, capital improvement, technology and parking fees $71.40 a credit = $1,715 — together MDC's own $4,831 a term — plus room and board $9,075 a term = $18,150. NO credit-load assumption was needed: MDC publishes 'Cost per Term (12 credits)' itself. ⚠ READ THE HOUSING LINE: MDC provides and supervises NO student housing, so the $18,150 is MDC's own living-independently allowance, NOT a college charge; it is stored under `roomBoard` because a player must still live in Miami and a tuition-only figure would badly mislead. ⚠ MDC's COA page says its figures are per term and should be doubled for a year, but its own 'Total' row doubles only the OTHER expenses and leaves tuition at one term — that total is internally inconsistent, so the components were doubled instead. Books ($1,500) and personal/transport are excluded by convention. The previous stored $11,000 was an unresearched ballpark and understated the cost by $16,812. The transfer pathway to Barry or FIU remains the value proposition, but Miami living costs are the story here, not tuition.

fin.internationalNote: Iowa Western non-resident/international direct billed cost $14,860 (Tier-1 verified from IWCC's official Paying for College costs page): tuition $230 a credit × 30 credits = $6,900 + college service fees $17 a credit = $510 + Village Double housing AND food $3,725 a semester = $7,450. NO credit-load assumption was needed — IWCC states that 'completing an associate's degree in 2 years requires a student to take 15 credits each semester', and its housing table says outright that the figures are 'the total costs for housing and food in each housing facility per semester'. IWCC charges internationals barely above the Iowa resident rate ($230 vs $225 a credit), which is why this stays one of the cheapest options in the guide. A Tower double (males only) is $3,300 a semester, $850 a year cheaper; singles run $4,380-$5,575 a semester. A one-time $35 first-enrolment fee and books (~$500 a semester) are excluded. The previous stored $14,000 was an unresearched ballpark and understated the cost by only $860 — the CLOSEST any ballpark came in the whole campaign. Athletic scholarships are available and the established Australian/European pipeline is real.

culture.vibe: Community college atmosphere — diverse student body from multiple backgrounds and ages. Iowa Western has a strong athletic culture — football is king in Iowa but soccer is growing. name: Murray State (OK)
degreeTitle: A.S. Health, Wellness & Human Performance (Athletic Training option)
acuAlignNote: Murray State's Associate of Science in Health, Wellness & Human Performance is a genuine 2-year exercise-science transfer degree rather than a generic transfer A.A. Mapped against the college's own 2025-26 degree check sheet: AP 1113 Applied Anatomy covers ANAT100; BIO 1114 General Biology covers BIOL125; HWP 2963 Introduction to Kinesiology covers EXSC224 (mechanical bases of movement); HWP 1011 Strength and Conditioning covers EXSC216; and PSY 2213 Wellness, Exercise, and Sports Psychology covers both EXSC199 and EXSC296. The gap that matters most for Olivier: the degree contains no exercise-physiology course at all, so EXSC225 and EXSC322 — two of the four units WES is most likely to credit directly — are NOT covered here, and neither is research methods (EXSC122). The program core does add HWP 2713 Care and Prevention of Athletic Injuries and HWP 2213 First Aid, both useful pre-PT context. An Athletic Training Option of the same degree swaps in HWP 2972 Athletic Training Practicum, which would add supervised clinical hours in the EXSC398 mould — worth raising with the program chair if pre-PT is the goal. Confirm all equivalences with an MSC advisor and a formal WES evaluation before transfer planning.

With a squad drawn from Brazil, France, Japan, Portugal, Trinidad, Morocco and beyond, the international players largely form their own social unit, and campus housing keeps everyone together. For a player who wants to focus for two years and then move up, the lack of distraction is arguably a feature.
culture.olivierMatch: ★★★ A strong sporting and financial match held back by location. The freshman-entry pathway is the most proven in the guide — an Australian from Sydney's northern beaches is on the current roster — the climate is mild, and the cost is among the lowest anywhere here. But Tishomingo is genuinely remote and small, with no city life, and the training environment lacks the S&C and sports-science support Olivier would get at a larger program. degreeTitle: A.S. Life Science (Pre-Professional option)
acuAlignNote: Eastern Oklahoma State's catalog (2025-26 Science & Mathematics degree plans) offers no dedicated Exercise Science or Kinesiology program — the closest fit is the A.S. in Life Science, Pre-Professional option, a genuine pre-health transfer track. Its required Natural Sciences general-education slot is satisfied by BIOL 1114 General Biology (covers BIOL125), and its 21-25 hour Pre-Professional Option block lets a student select five advisor-approved courses including BIOL 2114 Human Anatomy (covers ANAT100) alongside BIOL 2214 Human Physiology, Microbiology, Organic Chemistry and Nutrition. Full WES evaluation and advisor confirmation required before relying on this count.

acuAlignNote: Malcolm X College is City Colleges of Chicago's (CCC) designated Center of Excellence for Health Sciences (home to a $251M School of Health Sciences, opened 2016) and is the ONE CCC campus that actually teaches CCC's Exercise Sci and Sports Studies (ESSS) department, confirmed via the official district-wide academic catalog (catalog.ccc.edu/courses-az/esss/, every ESSS course tagged "Offered At: MX"). Real course-level matches against this guide's actual 16-unit rubric (js/app.js ACU_UNIT_META — checked by real definition, not by code name, per this campaign's Batch 4 lesson): ESSS 112 'Functional Anatomy & Kinesiology' (5cr — covers skeletal/muscular/nervous/circulatory anatomy AND 'locomotion, biomechanics, forces and levers') maps to ANAT100 (Anatomical Foundations), EXSC222 (Functional Anatomy) and EXSC224 (Mechanical Bases of Exercise / Intro Biomechanics) — three units from one course. ESSS 214 'Exercise and Health Psychology' maps to EXSC296 (Health & Exercise Psychology) specifically, NOT EXSC199 (Psychology of Sport / Sport Psychology) — ESSS214 covers general health-behavior psychology, stress and coping, not sport-specific psychology, so EXSC199 is marked false. ESSS 102 'Personal Trainer Practicum' (a supervised practical placement) maps to EXSC398 (Professional Experience). A general-education Life Sciences requirement covers BIOL125. No course maps to EXSC225 (a standalone Exercise Physiology course was not found — ESSS101 touches physiology only introductorily), EXSC322/EXSC394/EXSC321 (no advanced-level ESSS courses exist), EXSC204/EXSC216 (no dedicated exercise-testing/resistance-training course found), EXSC187/EXSC230/EXSC122 (no motor-development, motor-control or kinesiology-specific research-methods course found). Full WES evaluation and advisor confirmation required regardless.

The program's historical high point — a 2013 NJCAA DI Region 5 Championship and National Tournament berth — came under then-HC Jaime Beltran, now the founding head coach at already-guide Seward County CC. Ranger is a small, rural West Texas town offering real on-campus dormitory housing but no Exercise Science, Kinesiology, or Physical Education program of any kind. minutesOutlook is wide open: all 9 midfielders on the 2025-26 roster clear NJCAA eligibility before Olivier's Aug 2027 arrival.

jucoTierNote: A real coaching transition in progress: a respectable 2024-25 season (10-9-1 overall, .525) under the program's prior long-tenured staff gave way to a difficult 2025-26 debut for new HC Aron Bassoff (1-13-1, .100) — his first season rebuilding the roster. degreeTitle: A.S. in Health, Physical Education, and Recreation — Athletic Training Option
acuAlignNote: Northern Oklahoma College offers a genuine A.S. in Health, Physical Education, and Recreation with a dedicated Athletic Training Option, available at the Enid campus (confirmed via the college's own official 2025-2026 program curriculum PDF). Real required coursework includes BIOL 2104 Human Anatomy, BIOL 2204 Human Physiology, HPET 1113 Nutrition, HPET 1223 Health Education & Wellness, and HPET 2382/2482 Athletic Training Practicum I & II — a genuine clinical sequence totaling 75-85 hours of Year 1 observation plus 500 hours of Year 2 clinical work, among the most substantial clinical requirements found in this campaign. acuAlign scored 6, reflecting real anatomy/physiology and an unusually deep clinical-practicum component, offset by no dedicated Biomechanics, Resistance Training, or Sport Psychology course.

devScoresNote: Tier-1: HC Aron Bassoff (2nd season) brings one of the deepest coaching CVs found anywhere in this campaign — 19 seasons of intercollegiate coaching at the NCAA DII, NCAA DIII, and NAIA levels, 18 as a head coach (13 as a head men's coach), 7 nationally-ranked teams, 3 conference/regional championships, 11 second-place finishes, and 3 Conference Players of the Year produced, including a 47-22-6 record over 5 seasons at Davis & Elkins; he holds a B.S. in Sport and Exercise Science (Messiah College) and an M.S. in Sport Management (Nova Southeastern). The program's real standout asset is environmental: the $12 million Advance Soccer Complex (opened 2023) — a 1,500-seat championship artificial turf stadium plus six full-size natural turf practice/tournament fields and an indoor training complex with locker rooms, smart boards, and a training room — one of the best-documented JUCO soccer facilities found in this entire campaign. No dedicated strength & conditioning coach confirmed on the official staff directory.

rec: Northern Oklahoma College-Enid offers one of the best-documented soccer facilities found anywhere in this entire campaign — the $12 million Advance Soccer Complex, opened in 2023, features a 1,500-seat championship turf stadium, six full-size natural turf practice fields, and an indoor training complex — under HC Aron Bassoff, whose personal coaching CV (19 seasons, 18 as head coach, 3 conference/regional championships, a B.S. in Sport and Exercise Science) is one of the deepest in this guide. The program is in a genuine rebuild: Bassoff's debut 2025-26 season was difficult (1-13-1) following a respectable prior-staff 2024-25 (10-9-1), and his 2026-27 roster is almost entirely new. NOC-Enid pairs this with a genuine A.S. in Health, Physical Education, and Recreation (Athletic Training Option), including a real 500-hour clinical practicum sequence. Enid is a real regional Oklahoma city with an active local soccer community, though its Midwest climate is a poor match for Olivier's warm-climate preference. minutesOutlook reflects the program's genuine rebuild: only 1 of 10 midfielders on the current 2026-27 roster clears before Olivier's Aug 2027 arrival, with the other 9 (all freshmen) returning as sophomores to compete directly with him in his first season before the pool opens fully by his second year — the heaviest current-season midfield competition found anywhere in this batch.

minutesOutlook.trajectoryNote: NOC-Enid's own official 2026-27 roster (the current, already-published season, reflecting HC Aron Bassoff's near-total roster rebuild) lists 10 midfielders: 9 true freshmen who return as sophomores in 2027-28, directly competing with Olivier for minutes in his first season, and only 1 sophomore (Marco Segovia) who completes his 2-year NJCAA eligibility during 2026-27 and clears before Olivier's August 2027 arrival. The heaviest current-season midfield competition found in this batch — the pool opens fully only once the large freshman class completes its own eligibility at the end of 2027-28. Ask the coach: 'With nine returning sophomores in the midfield, what is the realistic path to minutes for an incoming freshman in 2027?'

recruit_pathway_note: The 2026-27 midfield pool is overwhelmingly true freshmen from a wide international base (Brazil, Serbia, Mexico, Morocco/France) with no transfer-portal annotation visible on the roster — the roster reads as a large true-freshman rebuild class rather than a portal-heavy roster, though the sheer size of the incoming class means genuinely heavy internal competition for an incoming recruit.
